scientific_question: Is the clean H1.16 zero-reward result caused primarily by the frozen 15-step action horizon rather than by carrier or adapter choice?
hypothesis: H1.16 traces show repeated next/back navigation and no buy transition. Extending only max_steps from 15 to 30 may reveal whether the frozen horizon is the limiting interface factor.
source_task_panel: H1.16 eight fresh task identities; no task or outcome enters training
cell_design: 2 conditions x 4 partitions x 8 attempts = 64 attempts; eight independent cells concurrent

resource_budget.gpu_policy: one independent UUID-bound cell per authorized GPU; no duplicate or occupancy-only work

stop_rule: one horizon-only diagnostic; no prompt rescue, memory, adapter, parser, or task changes

branch_rule.base30_positive: classify frozen horizon as a leading interface bottleneck; preregister the smallest interface follow-up, not Q3
branch_rule.both_negative: classify horizon as insufficient explanation; stop carrier/horizon micro-variants and inspect task/action interface under a new question
branch_rule.invalid: repair only runtime/provenance without changing horizon semantics

claim_boundary: Interface-horizon diagnosis only; no Q3, H2, D0, retention/transfer, or SEED claim.

oracle_reachability_audit.method: exact goal query plus deterministic target/options/buy actions; no model inference

result.next: Stop horizon, carrier, and adapter micro-variants; investigate task/action interface or model capability only under a new preregistered question. Keep Q3/H2/D0/retention/transfer/SEED closed.
